title: Vesti la giubba: Caruso, 1902 and 1907
work: Ruggero Leoncavallo: Recitar!… Vesti la giubba
question: What changes in Caruso’s lament when an orchestra takes the place of the piano?
intro: In Leoncavallo’s Pagliacci, Canio learns of his wife’s betrayal shortly before he has to perform as a clown for a paying audience. In the aria he orders himself to put on his costume and powder his face. Caruso recorded the aria with Salvatore Cottone at the piano in Milan in 1902, then with an orchestra in New York in 1907.

recordings.label: Enrico Caruso, Salvatore Cottone
recordings.note: In this Milan performance of 30 November 1902 the tenor is accompanied by one pianist, Cottone, who plays the whole accompaniment.

recordings.label: Enrico Caruso with orchestra
recordings.note: In the later Victor recording, made in New York, Canio’s lament is accompanied by an orchestra.

passages.label: Voice and piano
passages.note: The tenor sings Canio’s lament above the piano accompaniment. His words tell the clown to put on his costume.

passages.label: Rising and falling vocal line
passages.note: The vocal line rises and falls, and the accompaniment plays in the gaps between the tenor’s phrases.

passages.label: Final vocal phrases
passages.note: The tenor’s line rises again towards the aria’s final phrases over the accompaniment.

passages.label: Closing bars
passages.note: The last vocal phrases lead into the closing bars of the accompaniment.
